```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Analysis script accompanying: Osborne AK, Brown RD, Sillence E. Effects of Social Media Narratives on Affective and Behavioral Responses to Menopause Content: Randomized Online Experimental Study. *JMIR Form Res* 2026;10:e85788. doi:10.2196/85788

Place `Menopause_Social_Media_Study_Data.csv` in the same folder as this file and knit.

```{r}
# Rmisc attaches plyr, so it is loaded before dplyr; otherwise plyr::mutate masks
# dplyr::mutate and ignores group_by() when calculating within-condition percentages
library(Rmisc)
library(dplyr)
library(rmarkdown)
library(psych)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(MASS)
library(stringr)
```


# Set up and clean
```{r}
data <- read.csv("Menopause_Social_Media_Study_Data.csv")

# Remove the two Qualtrics header rows (question wording and import IDs)
data <- data[-c(1:2), ]

#convert to numeric values
cols_to_convert <- setdiff(names(data), c("Participant_ID", "FL_21_DO"))
data[cols_to_convert] <- lapply(data[cols_to_convert], function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x)))

# Inclusion criteria: consented, completed the survey, aged 40+.
# These were applied before the data were shared, so all 749 rows are retained here.
# The raw Qualtrics export (n = 781) also contained 18 screen-outs, 2 consent refusals,
# 10 incomplete/withdrawn responses (incl. 1 researcher test) and 2 participants aged
# under 40; these, and identifying fields (Prolific IDs, Qualtrics response IDs,
# timestamps), are not included in the shared data.
data <- subset(data, Finished != 0 & Age >= 40)
```

```{r}

data$time_taken_seconds <- data$Duration..in.seconds.
paged_table(describe(data$time_taken_seconds))

```



# Potential outliers
```{r}
#Condition groups
names(data)[names(data) == "FL_21_DO"] <- "Condition"
# Set Condition as a factor (Normal = reference) here, before the per-condition descriptives below
data$Condition <- as.factor(relevel(
  factor(str_trim(data$Condition, side = "both")),
  ref = "Normal"))
table(data$Condition)



#Outliers
cat(sum(data$Education > 20, na.rm = TRUE), "participants reported more than 20 years of post-16 education.\n")
cat(sum(data$time_taken_seconds < 150, na.rm = TRUE), "participants took under 2 1/2 minutes to complete the survey.\n")

data <- data[data$Education <= 20 ,]
data <- data[data$time_taken_seconds >= 150,]

#Attention check

cat("In response to the social media posts presented to each group", round((sum(data$N.Perceptions == 2, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(!is.na(data$N.Perceptions))) * 100, 2),
  "% of participants from the 'normal' condition reported that 'The posts portray menopause as a typical, natural stage of life.'\n")

cat(round((sum(data$T.Perceptions == 1, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(!is.na(data$T.Perceptions))) * 100, 2), "% of participants from the 'transformative' condition reported that 'The posts portray menopause as a significant and positive life change.'\n")

cat(round((sum(data$D.Perceptions == 3, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(!is.na(data$D.Perceptions))) * 100, 2), "% of participants from the 'distressing' condition reported that 'The posts portray menopause as difficult, negative, or overwhelming.'\n")

table(data$Condition
      )


```

# Visualisations
#### Affective response variables
```{r}
#combine affective responses, also adding feeling empowered and knowledgeable (from agreement section) as affective responses 
Affective_Responses <- data[, c("Affective_response_1","Affective_response_2","Affective_response_3","Affective_response_4", "Affective_response_5", "Affective_response_6", "Agreements_4","Agreements_5","Condition")]

names(Affective_Responses)[names(Affective_Responses) == "Agreements_4"] <- "Affective_response_7"
names(Affective_Responses)[names(Affective_Responses) == "Agreements_5"] <- "Affective_response_8"

Affective_Responses_long <- pivot_longer(Affective_Responses, cols = starts_with("Affective_response_"), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value")

Affective_Responses_means <- summarySE(data = Affective_Responses_long, measurevar = "Value", groupvars = c("Variable","Condition"), na.rm = TRUE, conf.interval = 0.95, .drop = TRUE)

Affective_Responses_means$Variable <- recode(
  Affective_Responses_means$Variable,
  "Affective_response_1" = "Worried",
  "Affective_response_2" = "Reassured",
  "Affective_response_3" = "Confused",
  "Affective_response_4" = "In control",
  "Affective_response_5" = "Optimistic",
  "Affective_response_6" = "Anxious",
  "Affective_response_7" = "Empowered",
  "Affective_response_8" = "Knowledgeable"
)
```

```{r}
Affective_plot <- ggplot(Affective_Responses_means) +
  aes(x = Variable, y = Value, colour = Condition) +
  geom_point(shape = "circle", size = 3L) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = Value - ci, ymax = Value + ci),
    width = 0.2,
    position = position_dodge(0.1)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    position = "right",
    limits = c(1, 5),
    breaks = 1:5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_text(aes(x = length(unique(Variable)) + 0.3, y = 5, label = "Strongly\nagree"), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(x = length(unique(Variable)) + 0.45, y = 4, label = "Agree"), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(x = length(unique(Variable)) + 0.45, y = 3, label = "Neither"), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(x = length(unique(Variable)) + 0.45, y = 2, label = "Disagree"), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(x = length(unique(Variable)) + 0.3, y = 1, label = "Strongly\ndisagree"), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "top"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Affective Response to Posts, by Condition",
    subtitle = "After reading the posts, to what extent do you agree you feel the following about menopause?",
    x = "Affective response",
    y = "Participant response",
    colour = "Condition"
  )

ggsave(
  "Affective_plot.png",
  plot = Affective_plot,
  device = "png",
  dpi = 300,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  bg = "white"
)

Affective_plot
```

# Model 1 - Predicting Affective Responses

```{r}
#Prepare variables
data$Condition <- as.factor(relevel(
  factor(str_trim(data$Condition, side = "both")),
  ref = "Normal"))

data$Worried <- as.factor(data$Affective_response_1)
data$Reassured <- as.factor(data$Affective_response_2)
data$Confused <- as.factor(data$Affective_response_3)
data$InControl <- as.factor(data$Affective_response_4)
data$Optimistic <- as.factor(data$Affective_response_5)
data$Anxious <- as.factor(data$Affective_response_6)
data$Empowered <- as.factor(data$Agreements_4)
data$Knowledgeable <- as.factor(data$Agreements_5)

```


```{r}
# Affective response variables
outcomes <- c("Worried", "Reassured", "Confused", "InControl", "Optimistic", "Anxious", "Empowered", "Knowledgeable")

get_model_results <- function(outcome_var) {
 
  formula <- as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~ Condition + scale(Age) + scale(Education) + scale(Social.Media)"))
  
  # Fit the proportional odds logistic regression
  model <- polr(formula, method = "logistic", Hess = TRUE, data = data)
  
  # Extract coefficients summary matrix
  coefs <- coef(summary(model))
  
  # Calculate p-values from t values
  p_vals <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(coefs[, "t value"])))
  
  # Add stars for p < 0.01
  stars <- ifelse(p_vals < 0.01, "*", "")
  
  # Dataframe
  results <- data.frame(
    Outcome = outcome_var,
    Term = rownames(coefs),
    Value = coefs[, "Value"],
    Std_Error = coefs[, "Std. Error"],
    t_value = coefs[, "t value"],
    p_value = round(p_vals, 10),
    Signif = stars,
    row.names = NULL
  )
  
  return(results)
}

# Run the function for all outcomes and bind results together
Affective_Results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(outcomes, get_model_results))

print(Affective_Results)
```

# Model 2 - Predicting Behavioural Responses
```{r}
# Prepare Behavioural response variables with renamed outcomes
data$Like <- as.factor(data$Behaviour_response_1)
data$Share <- as.factor(data$Behaviour_response_2)
data$Save <- as.factor(data$Behaviour_response_3)
data$Comment <- as.factor(data$Behaviour_response_4)
data$Search <- as.factor(data$Behaviour_response_5)
data$Discuss_w_friends_family <- as.factor(data$Discuss_posts_1)
data$Discuss_health_professional <- as.factor(data$Discuss_posts_2)
```

```{r}
# Define outcome variables
behaviour_outcomes <- c("Like", "Share", "Save", "Comment", "Search", 
                        "Discuss_w_friends_family", "Discuss_health_professional")

# Define function to run model and extract results
get_behaviour_model_results <- function(outcome_var) {
  
  formula <- as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~ Condition + scale(Age) + scale(Education) + scale(Social.Media)"))
  
  model <- polr(formula, method = "logistic", Hess = TRUE, data = data)
  
  coefs <- coef(summary(model))
  p_vals <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(coefs[, "t value"])))
  stars <- ifelse(p_vals < 0.01, "*", "")
  
  results <- data.frame(
    Outcome = outcome_var,
    Term = rownames(coefs),
    Value = coefs[, "Value"],
    Std_Error = coefs[, "Std. Error"],
    t_value = coefs[, "t value"],
    p_value = round(p_vals, 10),
    Signif = stars,
    row.names = NULL
  )
  
  return(results)
}

# Run for all outcomes and combine
Behaviour_Results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(behaviour_outcomes, get_behaviour_model_results))

# Print results
print(Behaviour_Results)

```

# Demographic effects

#### Affective responses
```{r}
# Affective response variables
outcomes <- c("Worried", "Reassured", "Confused", "InControl", 
              "Optimistic", "Anxious", "Empowered", "Knowledgeable")

data$Meno <- as.factor(data$Screening...Meno)

# Function to run models without Condition and filter for predictors only
get_demographics_only_results <- function(outcome_var) {
  
  formula <- as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~ scale(Age) + scale(Education) + scale(Social.Media) + Meno"))
  
  # Fit proportional odds logistic regression
  model <- polr(formula, method = "logistic", Hess = TRUE, data = data)
  print(rownames(coef(summary(model))))

  # Extract coefficients summary matrix
  coefs <- coef(summary(model))
  
  # Calculate p-values from t values
  p_vals <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(coefs[, "t value"])))
  
  # Add stars for p < 0.01
  stars <- ifelse(p_vals < 0.01, "*", "")
  
  # Format results
  results <- data.frame(
    Outcome = outcome_var,
    Term = rownames(coefs),
    Value = coefs[, "Value"],
    Std_Error = coefs[, "Std. Error"],
    t_value = coefs[, "t value"],
    p_value = round(p_vals, 10),
    Signif = stars,
    row.names = NULL
  )
  
  # Filter to only include predictor terms (exclude thresholds)
  results <- results[grepl("scale\\(|Meno", results$Term), ]  
  return(results)
}

# Run function for all affective outcomes
Affective_Demographics_Only <- do.call(rbind, lapply(outcomes, get_demographics_only_results))

# View or export
print(Affective_Demographics_Only)
# write.csv(Affective_Demographics_Only, "affective_demographics_filtered.csv", row.names = FALSE)


```
